items.title: Cognitive Engagement, Learning Strategies, Adjustment to College and Academic Motivation: A Structural Equation Model on Academic Success Among College Students
items.abstract: This study examined the relationships among cognitive engagement, learning strategies, adjustment to college, academic motivation, and academic success to determine the best-fit structural equation model among Bachelor of Elementary Education students in Region XIII (Caraga), Philippines. Anchored in Self-Regulated Learning Theory and Academic Adjustment Theory, the study employed a quantitative, non-experimental descriptive-correlational design involving 470 second-, third-, and fourth-year students from three state universities, selected through proportional stratified random sampling. Data were collected using five adapted, validated, and reliability-tested questionnaires and analyzed through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and structural equation modeling. Results revealed very high levels of cognitive engagement (M = 4.27), learning strategies (M = 4.32), college adjustment (M = 4.34), academic motivation (M = 4.32), and academic success (M = 4.31). All four predictors demonstrated significant positive correlations with academic success, with academic motivation exhibiting the strongest relationship (r = .519). The final structural model demonstrated excellent fit (CMIN/DF = .845, CFI = 1.000, RMSEA = .000) and explained 32.5% of the variance in academic success. Academic motivation (β = .270, p = .020) and learning strategies (β = .262, p = .017) emerged as significant direct predictors, whereas college adjustment and cognitive engagement showed nonsignificant direct effects. The findings emphasize the importance of strengthening academic motivation and effective learning strategies through learner-centered instruction and institutional support programs. The study supports Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education) by providing evidence to inform educational practices and student success initiatives. Its sustainability contribution lies in supporting evidence-based academic planning, student retention, and continuous improvement in higher education.

items.title: Commentary
items.abstract: This commentary examines the book and offers concluding remarks on healthy ageing and digital healthcare services in the Nordic countries. It identifies three key contributions and future directions. First, the compilation advances nuanced, strength-based representations of older adults’ engagement with digital technologies, challenging deficit-oriented accounts of ageing in a digital world. Second, it highlights the competences required by older care recipients and professionals in digitally mediated care, including domain-specific digital health literacy. Third, it questions assumptions that digital technologies straightforwardly promote independence and autonomy, situating care within wider sociotechnical networks of dependence, support, and responsibility. The commentary calls for holistic, critical, and interdisciplinary approaches to digital health care, attentive to misinformation, data privacy, security, and societal resilience.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models with SHAP Explanations towards Transparent Fake News Detection
items.abstract: The generation of fake news on online platforms has grown into a serious problem, compromising public trust, public opinion and the possibility of information-based decision making. In this study, an intelligent Fake News Detection (FND) system to automatically classify news articles as fake or real was developed using techniques of Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). A publicly available dataset consisting of 44,856 news articles from the LIAR data set and the Kaggle repository was used, of which 80% was used for training and 20% for testing. The data preprocessing included the following steps: Removing punctuation, Lowercase, Stop-word removal, Tokenization, Stemming, Lemmatization, and TF-IDF (Term Frequency – Inverse Document Frequency) Feature Extraction. The classification algorithms used were Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), which were trained and evaluated with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. Experimental results indicated that SVM outperforms the other models with respect to accuracy (99.21%), precision (99.25%), recall (99.23%), F1-Score (99.24%) and AUC-ROC (99.96%). To make the classifications auditable, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied uniformly to all five trained models rather than to the best model alone, permitting a direct comparison of the lexical evidence on which each classifier relies. The attributions converge: four of the five models rank the token “said” as the single most influential feature, and in every case, it shifts the prediction towards REAL, indicating that the models are detecting the attribution conventions of professional reporting rather than topic alone. The results show that the proposed NLP-ML-XAI framework is accurate, interpretable, and reliable for automatic fake news detection, which could be deployed by media organizations, fact checkers, and digital platforms to prevent spreading fake news online.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of the Technical and Operational Development of Unmanned Ground Vehicles Worldwide
items.abstract: Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) are one of the most prominent elements of the technological revolution that has been occurring in the defense sector over the past few years. The advent of asymmetric warfare, high-risk operational areas and the requirement for air platforms to operate with low human numbers has fueled the evolution of ground platforms for a variety of mission profiles. This study explores the different types of UGVs developed by countries in recent years based on technical and structural aspects. The mission types, locomotion configurations, power train systems, dimensions, weights, maximum speeds and operational endurance of the vehicles were comparatively evaluated. Platforms of the UGVs that are produced in some countries such as the United States, Germany, China, Russia, Estonia, Ukraine, Serbia and Türkiye were analyzed in this study. The results showed that for small-scale reconnaissance and surveillance vehicles, electric powered, lightweight wheeled systems are the predominant choice while heavy-duty vehicles such as assault and logistics vehicles are mostly hybrid or diesel powered tracked. The use of hybrid propulsion systems has increased due to the need for longer endurance and greater payload capacity for operational requirements. It was also found that there are big differences between the development methods of different countries. Where the United States is interested in platforms that are modular and can be adapted to specific missions, Russia is interested in heavily armed combat systems. China, on the other hand, concentrates on product diversity and cost-effective solutions. Türkiye has made outstanding strides in the development of medium and heavy class UGVs fitted with hybrid propulsion systems, assault and reconnaissance capabilities, and logistics capabilities, since 2018. The study finds that UGVs are progressing from remotely operated systems to artificial intelligence powered, modular, low-signature, multi-mission autonomous systems. Moreover, it is projected that swarm technologies, human–unmanned teaming, artificial intelligence-driven decision-making processes and hybrid energy technologies will be major contributors to the future designs and capabilities of UGVs.

items.title: COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS AND EXPLAINABILITY METHODS FOR ECG HEARTBEAT CLASSIFICATION
items.abstract: This study compared a 1D-CNN architecture and a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model for multiclass electrocardiographic heartbeat classification, incorporating Explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques to evaluate the faithfulness and temporal distribution of the evidence used by the models. Experiments used a dataset derived from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, organized into the Normal, Supraventricular, Ventricular, Fusion, and Unclassified classes. The protocol employed five-fold stratified cross-validation exclusively on the training set, epoch selection based on Macro F1 in an internal validation partition, and final evaluation on an untouched holdout test set. The 1D-CNN achieved a test Macro F1 of 0.8681 versus 0.8140 for the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model, whereas the hybrid model achieved higher Balanced Accuracy, 0.9441 versus 0.9264, indicating higher average class-wise recall. Explainability analysis employed 1D Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients, and temporal attention on a class-balanced subset of samples correctly classified by both architectures. Under the adopted perturbation protocol, Integrated Gradients showed positive mean faithfulness gains across all classes for both architectures, whereas Grad-CAM and temporal attention exhibited more class-dependent behavior. Low-to-moderate agreement among the methods indicated that different techniques may emphasize distinct temporal regions for the same correct prediction. Within this experimental setting, the additional complexity of the hybrid model did not translate into uniformly better predictive performance, supporting the complementary evaluation of predictive performance and explainability in ECG classification.

items.title: Comparing Genetic Algorithms and LLMs for Research-Hypothesis Generation: Mainstream Convergence of LLMs, Wider Hypothesis Exploration by Combinatorial Search, and the Limits of Literature-Distance Novelty Metrics
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based creative AI systems tend to produce plausible rather than novel research ideas. This study compares two ways of generating research hypotheses: a genetic algorithm (GA) that recombines Method, Problem, and Goal elements under a fitness function rewarding distance from the literature and literature support for each link, and free proposals by an LLM. Papers and hypotheses share one embedding space built from 2856 arXiv papers. Over 30 runs with budget-matched baselines and outcome measures on held-out and later-published papers, the selected hypotheses were more distant from the unseen literature than unsearched ones, but the GA matched rather than outperformed random search and hill climbing. Across two LLM families, two prompts, and two temperatures, and even when choosing from the GA’s concept vocabulary, LLM-proposed hypotheses were less diverse and closer to existing literature, whereas combinatorial search explored more widely. On 9755 ICLR submissions, the literature-distance novelty measure was practically unrelated to reviewers’ judgments (Spearman ρ ≤ 0.06), so it cannot establish originality. In controlled manuscript generation, LLM judges proved unreliable, and their order-consistent verdicts more often favored manuscripts built on LLM-proposed hypotheses, which blinded human raters tended to rank as least useful. Code and data are openly released.

items.title: Compensation–Skills Dual-Dimensional Configuration and Sustainable Upgrading of Export Technological Sophistication: A Re-Explanation of the “Value Paradox” of Skill Mismatch
items.abstract: Amid the restructuring of global value chains (GVCs) and the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution, how firms’ reallocation of human capital relates to escaping value chain lock-in has become a question of growing theoretical and practical importance for China. Traditional static skill-matching theory treats skill mismatch purely as a distortion in resource allocation. In the course of China’s industrial transformation and upgrading, the co-existence of configuration deviation and industrial upgrading is widely observed. Using panel data on Chinese listed firms from 2015 to 2023, this study measures firms’ relative configuration deviations along the compensation and skill dimensions against industry-year benchmarks. Different types of configuration deviation are then identified according to the sign combinations of deviations in these two dimensions. The results show that the overall magnitude of configuration deviation is not significantly associated with firms’ export technological sophistication (ETS). Instead, the direction and combination of deviations matter: firms with a High-high configuration are associated with significantly higher ETS than those in the reverse configuration. Decomposition by dimension shows that the Compensation-premium is significantly and positively associated with ETS but negatively associated with innovation output, whereas Skill-underutilization is positively associated with innovation yet negatively associated with contemporaneous ETS. Channel tests indicate that the High-high configuration is positively associated with two interconnected prospective channels: innovative-talent accumulation and AI orientation. No robust regional heterogeneity is identified in the association between the High-high and ETS. All coefficients of interest are interpreted as conditional associations estimated within a two-way fixed-effects framework, rather than as identified causal effects. Moving beyond the static job–skill matching paradigm, we interpret these findings through a dynamic capability-building lens and discuss sustainability-oriented policy implications for developing countries seeking to design differentiated talent and digital technology policies.

items.title: Composition determination of biodiesel/ethanol blends using dielectric spectroscopy and tabular prior-data fitted networks
items.abstract: Biodiesel/ethanol blends represent a promising alternative to reduce the consumption of fossil diesel. This work employs frequency-domain dielectric spectroscopy to determine the permittivity of biodiesel/ethanol blends across the full range of compositions, at temperatures between 293 K and 333 K, and within a frequency range from 1 MHz to 30 MHz. Within this interval, the real part of the permittivity is frequency-independent, and electrical losses are negligible. Leveraging these experimental results, a transformer-based deep learning model implementing Tabular Prior-data Fitted Networks (TabPFN) was developed to determine the blend composition from temperature and permittivity measurements. Evaluated via Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation, the proposed TabPFN model predicted the composition with high accuracy, yielding a coefficient of determination of 0.997, an average absolute deviation of 1.0 mol%, and a root mean squared error of 1.6 mol%. These results outperform conventional machine learning algorithms as well as standard analytical inversion models, operating in a single forward pass without requiring hyperparameter tuning or data scaling. Overall, using high-frequency dielectric spectroscopy together with tabular foundation models are the basis of a streamlined, highly efficient strategy for non-destructive biofuel quality verification.

items.title: Concept before capability - a validity-led approach to AI in OSCEs
items.abstract: Abstract Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) remain central to the assessment of clinical competence, yet the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into assessment design, delivery, and scoring raises a fundamental question: what evidence of competence are OSCEs intended to generate? This paper argues that AI should be evaluated through the lens of OSCE validity, with particular attention to how it may strengthen or weaken the interpretive chain linking observed performance to assessment decisions. Drawing on Messick’s unitary conception of validity and Kane’s argument-based framework, we examine how AI may introduce distinct threats across the scoring, generalisation, extrapolation, and implication inferences that underpin OSCE interpretation. We argue that generative AI (genAI) creates a particular risk of construct drift, whereby plausible assessment materials or scoring processes gradually reward observable proxies rather than the underlying clinical capabilities they are intended to assess. To translate this validity perspective into practice, we propose a framework that maps AI applications across the OSCE workflow according to their proximity to candidate consequences and the evidential burden required to justify their use. Lower-risk applications, such as design support and post-hoc analytics, may strengthen assessment when accompanied by construct-focused review and human oversight, whereas higher-risk uses, including AI-mediated candidate encounters and automated summative scoring, require substantially stronger validity evidence. We conclude that AI should be adopted according to the principle of concept before capability: assessment communities must first establish what clinical competence means and what evidence should count before deciding where AI has a legitimate role in high-stakes assessment.

items.title: Conceptualising Digital Transformation Through Recursive Capability Constriction: Evidence from Australian NDIS Providers
items.abstract: Digital transformation is a strategic priority across care-intensive service sectors, yet many organisations struggle to realise its intended benefits. Existing research often examines technological, organisational, and environmental barriers separately, offering limited insight into their interconnections within organisational systems. Drawing on Systems Theory and Sociotechnical Systems (STS) Theory, this study investigates digital transformation among small and medium providers within Australia’s National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS). Using an interpretive qualitative design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 participants from 15 distinct NDIS provider organisations in Sydney, Australia, followed by reflexive thematic analysis and systems-oriented interpretation. Participants described recurring associations among technological misalignment, fragmented software, adaptive workarounds, increased administrative demands, and constraints on organisational capacity for digital improvement, with regulatory and resource pressures interacting with these technological and organisational conditions. Building on these cross-sectional patterns, this study develops Recursive Capability Constriction (RCC), a systems-based conceptual framework that proposes how technological misalignment, compensatory adaptation, administrative expansion, and constrained organisational capability for digital improvement may become interconnected through reinforcing relationships. Rather than representing an inevitable or empirically established causal sequence, RCC provides a conditional explanation of how local adaptations may become associated with constraints on subsequent digital improvement. By shifting attention from isolated implementation barriers to interconnected sociotechnical relationships, RCC extends digital transformation research and provides practical guidance for managing digital change in regulated care environments.

items.title: Confidence without consensus? Human versus AI abstracts in urology
items.abstract: Abstract Objective This study asked whether urologists can tell human-written abstracts apart from artificial intelligence (AI)-written abstracts when both describe the same study, and whether the answer depends on which AI model did the writing. Methods Fifteen published urology studies were selected. For each study, the original human-written abstract was paired with three AI-written abstracts covering the same material, produced by Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5, and Gemini 3 Flash using identical instructions and each model’s ordinary consumer settings. Because all four versions described the same study, the underlying data were held constant, and the versions differed in how that material was written and presented. The resulting 60 abstracts were stripped of identifying information, and eight urologists read all of them without knowing which was which (480 judgments in total). For each abstract, reviewers stated whether they believed it was written by a human or by AI, rated how confident they were in that judgment, and rated the abstract’s quality and credibility on 5-point scales. Results Reviewers correctly identified AI-written abstracts 49.3% of the time, approximately 50%, compared with 62.4% for human-written abstracts ( p = .011). Results depended heavily on which model wrote the text ( p = .003). Abstracts written by Claude were recognized as AI only 40.0% of the time, significantly less often than human abstracts were correctly identified ( p = .003) and less often than GPT abstracts (56.8%, p = .038); Gemini fell between the two at 50.9%. Quality ratings differed only for GPT, which scored lower than human abstracts ( p = .046; omnibus p = .030); credibility ratings did not differ between sources at all ( p = .577). Reviewers who felt confident were no more likely to be correct ( p = .749), and reviewers seldom agreed with one another about which abstracts were AI-written (Fleiss’ κ = −0.009). Conclusion Urologists could not reliably recognize AI-written urology abstracts, and the difficulty came mainly from one model rather than from AI writing in general. How good an abstract appeared had little to do with whether its authorship was correctly identified, and neither reviewer confidence nor agreement between reviewers gave any warning. Reading alone is therefore not a dependable way to detect undisclosed AI authorship.

items.title: Connectivity optimization of artificial neural network with evolutionary computation algorithms
items.abstract: Human intelligence has historically produced various solutions to the challenges it has faced thanks to its cognitive abilities such as learning, remembering, comparing, and problem-solving. One of the most fundamental examples of artificial intelligence approaches that emerged by modeling these behaviors specific to intelligence is the artificial neural network (ANN), inspired by the biological nervous system. ANNs, with their similarity to biological nervous systems, present a highly complex system, and with technological advancements, the modeling and applicability of these systems are constantly increasing. In this study, a new ANN architecture inspired by the biological nervous system was designed. To improve the classification performance of the developed architecture, the connections in the network were treated as a binary optimization problem and optimized using the Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO) algorithm. Following the architecture design, the weights of the connections in the network were optimized using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm which works with continuous values. As a result, a network architecture compatible with the biological nervous system, flexible in structure, and highly applicable to various problem types was created. The developed method was tested on Breast Cancer, Hepatitis, Mammographic Mass and Haberman’s Survival datasets. Additionally, proposed model compared with the Genetic Algorithm (GA), one of the most widely used evolutionary computation methods in the literature for connection optimization. Specifically, the proposed model reduces the input layer size from 5 to 2 in the Mammographic Mass domain by applying aggressive feature selection. It successfully reduces computational complexity by eliminating up to 12 hidden neurons in the Hepatitis dataset without sacrificing classification accuracy, thus providing significant structural pruning. Furthermore, it demonstrates high stability across all metrics with minimal standard deviation, proving that the synergy between binary and continuous swarm variants generates highly concise, lightweight, and efficient neural network topologies

items.abstract: The horticultural production model has shown structural weaknesses under current environmental and production conditions. This study aims to analyze the trajectory of construction and expansion of the No-Till Vegetable System (NTVS) in the Metropolitan Region of Porto Alegre (MRPA), Brazil, between 2018 and 2025, based on a qualitative-quantitative action research approach. The process was developed in interaction with family farmers, integrating teaching, research, and extension activities. The results indicate that SPDH is not characterized by the adoption of isolated techniques, but as a gradual process of reorganizing production systems, conditioned by ecological, operational, and structural limitations. Competition with spontaneous plants, nutritional imbalance, and lack of appropriate mechanization were identified as major constraints. Conversely, the participatory development of technologies and the role of sociotechnical networks supported system construction. It is concluded that agroecological transition depends on the articulation between knowledge, material conditions, and social organization.

items.title: Context presentation and native conversation structure in large language model responses to escalating suicide risk: a controlled multimodel evaluation
items.abstract: Background Large language models are increasingly used for informal mental health support, yet their safety during escalating suicide-risk conversations may depend on how prior information is presented. Native multi-turn conversations and reconstructed cumulative prompts differ not only in the presence of prior model responses but also in prompt reconstruction, information concentration, message positioning, explicit integration cues, and conversation-state processing. Objective This study compared suicide-risk recognition, direct safety inquiry, response urgency, and timely real-world intervention across isolated current-turn prompts, reconstructed cumulative user-only prompts, and native continuous multi-turn conversations. Methods We conducted a controlled repeated-measures evaluation of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao using 12 standardized five-turn trajectories: 4 direct suicide-risk trajectories, 4 implicit or internally inconsistent risk trajectories, and 4 non-suicidal high-distress controls. Each trajectory was evaluated under three context-presentation formats. The 24 model-trajectory combinations were treated as matched repeated-measures units nested within 8 independent risk-trajectory blocks. Primary contrasts were estimated using exact trajectory-level sign-flip tests and trajectory-block bootstrap confidence intervals. Turn-level outcomes were analyzed using multilevel mixed-effects models. Exploratory condition-by-model heterogeneity was assessed using a trajectory-blocked exact permutation sensitivity analysis, with a trajectory-clustered interaction model used only as a secondary asymptotic check. Results Timely appropriate intervention occurred in 10/24 isolated current-turn observations (41.7%), 21/24 reconstructed cumulative observations (87.5%), and 12/24 native continuous observations (50.0%). On average across the three systems, reconstructed cumulative presentation exceeded isolated input by 45.8 percentage points (95% trajectory-block bootstrap CI, 25.0 to 66.7; Holm-adjusted exact P = .031), whereas native continuous performance was 37.5 percentage points lower than reconstructed cumulative performance (95% trajectory-block bootstrap CI, −50.0 to −25.0; Holm-adjusted exact P = .031). Exploratory model-specific analyses indicated substantial heterogeneity: the native-versus-reconstructed contrast was largest for Doubao, smaller and statistically imprecise for Gemini, and absent for ChatGPT. Conclusions On average across the three evaluated systems, reconstructed cumulative user-only prompts outperformed native continuous conversations, although exploratory model-specific patterns were heterogeneous. Because the formats also differed in prompt reconstruction, information salience, message positioning, explicit integration instructions, and native conversation-state processing, the contrast cannot isolate the causal effect of prior model responses.

items.title: Context sensitivity in ChatGPT–generated peer review: evaluative alignment across positive and negative user-provided contexts
items.abstract: Introduction Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support evaluative tasks, raising questions about whether their judgements remain independent when users provide prior evaluative information. This study examined the context sensitivity of GPT-5.5 Instant-generated academic peer-review evaluations under positive and negative user-provided evaluative contexts. Method Sixteen academics evaluated two published manuscripts, classified for the study as relatively higher and lower quality, across four structured conditions. Each participant completed all conditions in separate ChatGPT sessions, yielding 64 peer-review outputs. Descriptive summaries of overall scores and publishability judgements complemented qualitative content analysis. Results Three themes emerged: alignment of evaluative emphasis with user-provided evaluative context, differences in the relative prominence of evaluation criteria, and explicit alignment with the user-provided evaluation. Mean ChatGPT scores were 8.74 and 8.84 under positive evaluative context, compared with 3.37 and 3.64 under negative evaluative context for the lower- and higher-quality manuscripts, respectively. Discussion Because all evaluative inputs included both a verbal evaluation and a numerical rating, the findings reflect sensitivity to the broader evaluative context and do not distinguish the contribution of verbal framing from numerical anchoring. The results highlight a potential limitation in treating ChatGPT-generated evaluations under comparable interaction conditions as independent second opinions and underscore the importance of interaction design in human–AI evaluation workflows.

items.title: Context-Aware And Explainable Hate Speech Detection In Iraqi Social Media: A Framework For Parliamentary And Policy Analysis
items.abstract: Overview: Concerns about hate speech and its implications for social cohesion, public discourse, and the safety of targeted communities have been intensified by the rapid expansion of social media, particularly in Iraq owing to its social, cultural, and linguistic diversity, as well as its experience of severe sectarian conflict and communal violence during 2006–2007. Hence, it is important to examine social cohesion and harmful intergroup discourse in contemporary digital environments without assuming a direct causal relationship between past conflict and present-day online hate speech. Gap: Machine learning and Transformer-based hate-speech detection frameworks have significantly advanced in recent times; however, the reliable identification of hate speech in Iraqi social-media discourse remains challenging since online communication in the country often involves dialectal variation, informal and non-standard spelling, code-mixing, sarcasm, implicit and coded expressions, and deliberate linguistic obfuscation. These context-dependent and dialect-sensitive characteristics may not be adequately captured by generic language representations, and classification performance alone may fail to provide enough insight into model explainability, generalization across different forms of Iraqi online discourse, and robustness to linguistic manipulation. Hence, there is a need for a framework that can combine contextual understanding, dialect sensitivity, explainability, and robustness for the Iraqi context. Contributions: A context-aware and explainable hate-speech detection framework has been proposed in this study for deployment across Iraqi social media; the methodology of the proposed framework dynamically combines contextual and dialect-specific information for hate-speech classification by integrating Iraqi-aware text preprocessing, contextual Transformer representations, dialect-sensitive feature learning, and an adaptive fusion mechanism. The system also incorporates Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for identifying the linguistic elements contributing to model predictions; robustness analysis evaluates model behavior under realistic linguistic variations and obfuscation strategies. In addition to the computational contribution, an interdisciplinary AI–policy framework is also incorporated, wherein anonymized and aggregated hate-speech patterns can provide empirical evidence for parliamentary and public-policy analysis. The legislative and oversight role of the Iraqi Council of Representatives in addressing online hate speech was also examined in consideration of freedom of expression, privacy, explainability, responsible digital governance, and human oversight. Conclusion: An integrated approach that connects Iraqi-contextualized hate-speech detection with explainable and robust artificial intelligence and parliamentary policy analysis has been proposed in this study, wherein AI is positioned as an empirical research and decision-support instrument rather than a mechanism for automated censorship, punishment, or legal determination. A combination of linguistic adaptation, contextual modeling, explainability, robustness assessment, and aggregated policy-oriented evidence in the proposed methodology provides an experimentally testable and socially responsible foundation for analyzing hate speech in Iraqi social media and supporting evidence-informed parliamentary and public-policy analysis.

items.title: Controlled Evidence Mapping of Digitally Enabled Climate-Smart Tourism: From Fragmented Applications to Integrated Destination Climate Intelligence
items.abstract: This study maps the knowledge structure of AI-enabled climate-smart tourism and examines how artificial intelligence, digital twins, the Internet of Things, remote sensing, predictive analytics, and climate services support adaptation, mitigation, and destination resilience. A systematic evidence-mapping design was combined with controlled bibliometric science mapping. Following PRISMA 2020 and SPAR-4-SLR, 77 records were screened, yielding 50 eligible publications available through June 2026. Analyses included concept co-occurrence, temporal overlay, technology–function cross-tabulation, climate-relevance coding, and evidence-maturity assessment. Publication activity increased after 2023, with planning and governance dominating the literature. Only 11 studies explicitly addressed climate risk, adaptation, weather, or resilience, while outcome-level evaluation remained limited. The findings reveal a sensing-to-action gap, as observation, prediction, simulation, implementation, and learning are rarely integrated. The study conceptualizes AI-enabled climate-smart tourism as an outcome-oriented destination capability and proposes a six-stage climate-intelligence cycle connecting sensing, integration, prediction, simulation, decision-making, adaptation, and learning.

items.title: Corporate ethical and responsible AI (CERAi) and AI trustworthiness: a lifecycle perspective and empirical insights
items.abstract: Purpose This study develops and empirically validates a Corporate Ethical and Responsible AI (CERAi) lifecycle framework. The framework comprises three interdependent stages: design and development, testing and training, and deployment and usage. The study aims to move the research beyond abstract principles and policy analyses toward empirically grounded, lifecycle-integrated artificial intelligence AI governance theory. It positions ethical AI and responsible AI governance as the two constitutive components of the CERAi construct, and AI trustworthiness as a conceptually and empirically distinct downstream outcome anchored in stage-specific organizational governance mechanisms. The CERAi framework is scoped broadly to encompass governance of both conventional/traditional machine learning models and autonomous AI agents operating within organizational settings. Design/methodology/approach We administered a large-scale survey to 500 attendees at a national AI conference in the United States in early 2026, yielding 143 useable responses from AI professionals across healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, retail and energy sectors. We developed and validated multi-item scales for each CERAi lifecycle stage using established ethical AI and AI governance frameworks. Structural equation modeling was employed to assess the measurement model and to test both direct path hypotheses and mediation hypotheses. Findings Both CERAIi design and development and CERAi deployment and usage have significant positive direct effects on AI trustworthiness, whereas CERAi testing and training do not. Our results also indicate a significant serial mediation pathway in which CERAi deployment and usage enhance AI trustworthiness through testing and training, followed by design and development. Conversely, testing and training alone do not mediate the relationship between deployment and usage and AI trustworthiness, indicating that design-stage ethics serve as an intervening (mediating) mechanism through which governance activity enacted at later lifecycle stages is associated with perceived AI trustworthiness. This is consistent with testing and training's association with trustworthiness operating indirectly, mediated by the ethical architecture established during the design and development stage. Originality/value Findings of this study demonstrate that AI trustworthiness reflects differentiated perceived salience across AI lifecycle stages, whereby stakeholders appear to weight visible, deployment-stage governance more heavily than upstream design and testing stage governance in forming trustworthiness judgments, rather than reflecting a definitive validation that governance effects accumulate uniformly across all stages in isolation. This study makes a distinctive contribution by providing empirical evidence for a governance-sequencing mechanism, whereby design-stage ethics function as a mediating pathway shaping the effectiveness of governance activity at later lifecycle stages. To the best of our knowledge, such a mediated, stage-sequential mechanism has not previously been demonstrated using primary data within a comprehensive, three-stage CERAi lifecycle framework linking organizational ethical and responsible governance practices to AI trustworthiness outcomes.

items.title: Corporate social responsibility and employee motivation: intrinsic and extrinsic pathways in Vietnamese SMEs
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to conceptualize corporate social responsibility (CSR) as a potentially need-supportive organizational context. This study examines how CSR-related autonomy, competence and relatedness are associated with employees’ intrinsic and extrinsic motivation and how these two forms of motivation are subsequently associated with perceived work performance and job engagement among employees of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Self-Determination Theory, this study analyzed survey data collected from 379 employees working in SMEs in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings CSR-specific competence and relatedness were positively linked to both intrinsic and extrinsic motivation. Autonomy, by contrast, was positively associated with intrinsic motivation but showed no significant association with extrinsic motivation. Intrinsic motivation was positively associated with perceived work performance, while both extrinsic motivation and perceived work performance were positively associated with job engagement. Originality/value This study advances employee-centered CSR research in an underexplored emerging-market SME context. This study offers guidance on CSR design choices that prioritize competence development and social connectedness to strengthen employee outcomes.

items.title: Crafting Resilient AI policies for Education
items.abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence into academic spaces requires a shift from passive restriction to resilient, active pedagogical frameworks. This virtual panel explores actionable strategies to protect academic integrity, promote deep critical thinking, and manage AI use, particularly in foundational courses. Panelists will discuss the implementation of high-engagement classroom interventions. The will offer frameworks for transparent student disclosure practices. Attendees will leave with practical templates for syllabus policies, assignment rubrics, and disclosure benchmarks designed to foster a culture of transparency and process-oriented learning in an AI-permeated landscape.

items.title: Crossing the Digital Divide: Understanding Older Adults’ Technology Acceptance of Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Qualitative Study
items.abstract: The diffusion of generative artificial intelligence is redefining the relationship between older adults and digital technologies. Existing studies have largely explained the digital divide among older adults through traditional digital media such as smartphones and mobile payment, while insufficient attention has been paid to how conversational artificial intelligence changes older adults' entry thresholds, sustained-use motivations, and risk-judgment mechanisms. This study adopts a multimethod qualitative design, with semistructured interviews as the primary method and digital scenario-based tasks as a complementary method. From January to February 2026, the study was conducted in Chedun Town and Xinqiao Town, Songjiang District, Shanghai, with 40 participants aged 60 and above who had internet-use experience and showed a pronounced tendency toward high-frequency smartphone use. The data were analyzed through thematic analysis. Interview transcripts, task-observation records, screenshots of AI conversations, and field notes were triangulated; an initial coding manual, double review, and consensus discussion were used to enhance analytic credibility. The study finds that generative artificial intelligence shifts the technological threshold from procedural operation to need articulation and result evaluation, enabling some older adults to compensate for limitations in traditional interface operation through life experience and language-expression skills. Older adults' sustained use is not driven simply by efficiency, but is closely related to emotional anchoring in later life, experience organization, relationship maintenance, and concrete task handling. Community support, peer learning, and intergenerational assistance constitute important mediating mechanisms through which older adults move from initial experimentation to stable use. Whether older adults truly cross the digital divide depends on whether they can develop the capacities of source verification, contextual delimitation, and boundary judgment. Based on these findings, the study proposes a "conditional crossing" mechanism for older adults' acceptance of AI technologies and argues that age-friendly governance should move beyond interface simplification toward capability enhancement and risk support.

items.title: Cuando la ciudad habla: Patrimonio y participación ciudadana como agentes de cambio en las tareas de hacer ciudad
items.abstract: Participation can be defined as a social practice in which every individual, by taking part in public events, builds identity, a sense of ownership and belonging; qualities that are inherently linked to heritage, as it serves as the vessel of a people’s collective memory. Therefore, citizen participation and heritage share attributes that, when combined, could have a positive impact on the management of historic cities. Despite the introduction of legislative changes aimed at making participation more flexible, much remains to be done in practice. Although there are efforts to incorporate the voice of citizens into plans and programmes, it is often the case that the human factor sustaining our historic cities is neither acknowledged in regulations nor allowed to participate actively in urban transformation models. Participation constitutes a complex scenario, but it must begin to be addressed in a real, practical and effective manner, so that all social actors can work together in developing proposals that move beyond the tensions between tradition and modernity, nostalgia and oblivion, ultimately leading to vibrant, diverse, inclusive and sustainable city centres.

items.title: Customer complaint analytics in digital financial services: temporal prediction of untimely responses and capacity-aware prioritization
items.abstract: Abstract Digital financial service providers often receive more customer complaints than can be examined through intensive review and individualized handling. Prior research has examined technology adoption, service quality, satisfaction, trust, loyalty, and artificial intelligence in finance, but less is known about how complaint records can support transparent prioritization when review capacity is limited. This study develops a customer complaint analytics framework for capacity-constrained digital financial services using public Consumer Financial Protection Bureau records. Because realized churn, customer lifetime value, intervention histories, and treatment effects are unavailable, the empirical target is not customer defection or a proxy constructed from complaint text. Instead, the study predicts an independently observed post-intake service process outcome: whether the company subsequently provides an untimely response. The final analytical sample contains 266,337 complaints received between January 2024 and April 2026. Model development is restricted to 2024–2025 through three blocked temporal validation folds, while January–April 2026 is reserved as an untouched final holdout. Structured attributes, sparse lexical features, and fixed dense semantic embeddings are compared under the same temporal design, with mean development average precision (AP) used for model selection. The selected term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF–IDF) logistic model achieves a final holdout area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC) of 0.7653 and AP of 0.04985. Within the highest ranked 10% of complaints, precision is 4.83% against a holdout prevalence of 1.24%, corresponding to a lift of 3.89 and capture of 38.94% of all untimely responses. The study therefore shows that intake time complaint information contains predictive signal available at intake for identifying complaints that later receive untimely company responses and can support capacity-aware early review. These results should not be interpreted as evidence of customer churn, retention effects, consumer harm, or causal service recovery benefit.

items.title: Cybersecurity Awareness and Digital Literacy for Students and Educators Strengthening Data Privacy with AI-Powered Cybersecurity
items.abstract: This study aims to investigate the significance of cybersecurity awareness, digital literacy, and artificial intelligence in fostering data privacy protection for students and teachers in North India. The study was an exploratory descriptive study with a cross-sectional quantitative design, based on primary data gathered from a structured questionnaire with 620 respondents. The methods used were descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression. The correlation was positive for all of the variables, and the highest was between the AI-driven cybersecurity and data privacy protection (r = .741, p < .001). The results of the regression showed that artificial intelligence cybersecurity, digital literacy and cyber security awareness had significant predicting power for data privacy protection, accounting for 66.3% of its variance. The results highlight the need for a holistic approach to integrating AI into education, fostering digital literacy, and raising cybersecurity awareness to ensure safer and privacy-conscious learning spaces.

items.title: Dark Pattern Finder for Consumer Protection Web Extension
items.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce platforms and web-based services has increased the use of user interface techniques designed to influence online decision-making. Among these techniques, dark patterns are deceptive or manipulative design practices that can mislead users, encourage unintended actions, or make it difficult to understand and control their choices. Identifying such patterns manually across different websites is time-consuming and requires considerable awareness of deceptive interface designs. To address this challenge, this project titled “Dark Pattern Finder” presents an intelligent browser-based system that automatically detects and identifies potential dark patterns present in web pages.The proposed system utilizes Artificial Intelligence and machine learning techniques to analyze webpage content and identify suspicious interface patterns. A browser extension collects relevant webpage information, including DOM elements, visible text, user interactions, and other behavioral evidence. The collected information is processed by a backend detection system developed using Python and FastAPI. A machine learning-based classification model analyzes the extracted content and categorizes potential dark patterns such as scarcity and urgency, deceptive messages, forced actions, and other manipulative interface practices. The system also provides confidence scores and supporting evidence to improve the transparency and interpretability of the detection results.To enhance the reliability of detection, the proposed system integrates multiple analysis approaches, including DOM-based analysis, behavioral observation, and state-change information. The detected patterns are presented directly through the browser extension using visual overlays and user-friendly notifications, enabling users to understand potentially manipulative elements while browsing. The system can also associate detected patterns with relevant legal and regulatory information to provide additional awareness regarding potentially deceptive practices.

items.title: Data Analysis Using LLMs: Tools, Sandboxes and Data Agents
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to support data analysis and have the potential to make statistical methods more accessible to clinicians and medical researchers with limited programming experience. However, the rapid development of technologies surrounding LLMs has introduced new concepts and workflows that may be unfamiliar to potential users. In particular, tool calling, sandboxing, and data science agents provide different mechanisms through which LLMs can perform statistical analyses, yet the distinctions between these approaches are often unclear. This paper introduces and compares these three developments from the perspective of statistical data analysis. Tool calling allows an LLM to access predefined statistical functions, sandboxing provides a controlled computational environment in which model-generated code can be executed, and data science agents extend these capabilities by combining reasoning, tools, memory, planning, and execution environments to pursue analytical objectives through multi-step workflows. Their application is illustrated using the R programming language together with the ellmer and securer packages. Examples demonstrate how statistical analyses can be performed using predefined functions, code execution within a sandbox, and a simple biostatistics agent. The advantages, limitations, and verification requirements of each approach are discussed, with particular emphasis on transparency, reproducibility, and human oversight. This paper aims to provide clinicians, researchers, and statisticians with an accessible introduction to these emerging technologies and their potential role in LLM-assisted data analysis.

items.title: Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted great attention in both academic and industrial communities in recent years. Numerous survey studies have covered various aspects of LLMs, such as learning strategies, applications, alignment, explainability, and evaluation. However, little headway has been made in reviewing data-related aspects for LLMs, despite data being recognized as a key factor contributing to the emergence of the LLMs era. A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs' training and application processes. These techniques often originate from diverse deep learning domains, with their theoretical inspirations and heuristic motivations appearing unrelated to each other. This study aims to develop a comprehensive framework for LLMs' data optimization techniques to enhance data utilization efficiency. We first discuss data challenges in LLMs' training and inference. Second, we summarize data perception dimensions for evaluating LLMs' data properties. Third, existing optimization techniques are reviewed and categorized into four groups: data selection, augmentation, reweighting, and others. Fourth, we analyze interconnections between these categories. Finally, we identify key challenges and future directions for LLMs' data optimization compared with conventional deep learning approaches.

items.title: DEEP LEARNING APPLICATIONS IN BRAIN TUMOR CLASSIFICATION ON MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING: A DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY STUDY
items.abstract: Background: Brain tumours are among the most challenging neurological disorders due to their diverse histopathological characteristics and overlapping imaging features.Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is the preferred imaging modality for the evaluation of brain tumours because of its superior soft-tissue contrast and multiplanar imaging capability.However, accurate tumor classification remains dependent on radiologist expertise and may be subject to interobserver variability.Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have shown promising results in automated image analysis and tumor classification, with the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making. Aim: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of deep learning applications in the classification of brain tumours on Magnetic Resonance Imaging.Objectives:1. To determine the diagnostic accuracy of a deep learning model for classifying brain tumours on MRI using histopathological diagnosis as the reference standard.2. To compare the diagnostic performance of the deep learning model with radiologist interpretation in the classification of brain tumours on MRI. Materials and Methods:A hospital-based diagnostic accuracy study was conducted in the Department of Radiodiagnosis in collaboration with the Departments of Neurosurgery and Pathology.A total of 30 patients with histopathologically confirmed brain tumours who fulfilled the inclusion and exclusion criteria were included.Preoperative MRI examinations were analysed using a validated deep learning algorithm.The deep learning predictions were compared with histopathological diagnosis, which served as the gold standard, and with conventional radiologist interpretation.Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, overall accuracy, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, area under the curve (AUC), Cohen's kappa coefficient, and McNemar's test.A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results:The mean age of the study participants was 44.8 ± 13.2 years, with a male predominance (56.7%).Glioma was the most common tumor (40.0%), followed by meningioma (26.7%), pituitary adenoma (16.7%), brain metastasis (10.0%), and other tumors (6.6%).The deep learning model correctly classified 27 of the 30 cases.The model demonstrated a sensitivity of 93.3%, specificity of 86.7%, positive predictive value of 87.5%, negative predictive value of 92.9%, and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 90.0%.The area under the ROC curve was 0.94, indicating excellent diagnostic performance.Comparison with histopathology showed no statistically significant difference (McNemar test, p = 0.564).The deep learning model also demonstrated slightly higher sensitivity, specificity, overall accuracy, and agreement with histopathology than conventional radiologist interpretation, although the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.317). Conclusion:Deep learning demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance in the classification of brain tumours on MRI and showed strong agreement with histopathological diagnosis.It performed comparably to conventional radiologist interpretation and may serve as a valuable clinical decision-support tool for improving diagnostic accuracy, reducing observer variability, and facilitating timely treatment planning.Larger multicentre studies with standardized imaging protocols are recommended to further validate these findings before routine clinical implementation.

items.title: Design Thinking for Mathematical Critical Thinking in Digital Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Mathematical critical thinking in digital learning requires purposeful interaction among pedagogical tasks, digital tools, and students' interpretation and justification of mathematical ideas. This systematic literature review examines the complementary functions of GeoGebra, Problem-Based Learning (PBL), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Meaningful Learning, and Design Thinking. The manuscript reports a qualitative thematic synthesis of 15 primary empirical studies published within the 2020–2026 search period and identified through Scopus, ERIC, Google Scholar, DOAJ, and Garuda. The available reporting record does not preserve complete database-specific retrieval and screening counts or item-level methodological appraisal results; the review therefore does not claim a fully reproducible PRISMA 2020 selection record. Across the cited evidence, GeoGebra provides dynamic mathematical representations; PBL structures problem-centred inquiry; AI offers feedback and alternative approaches that require mathematical verification; and Meaningful Learning emphasizes connections with prior knowledge. Design Thinking is proposed as a learner-centred organizing process through Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test. These differentiated functions support a conceptually coherent, potentially testable instructional pathway rather than a demonstrated effect of the combined intervention. Future research should verify the primary-study corpus, document review procedures in full, and test the proposed relationships in classroom settings.

items.title: Designing Custom Chatbots for Classroom Use: Practical Examples, Benefits, and Current Limitations
items.abstract: Recent advances in generative AI have made it increasingly possible for individual educators to design and implement their own custom chatbots without advanced programming skills (Abe & Kaneshige, 2025). This workshop introduces practical examples of custom chatbots developed for educational purposes and discusses both their affordances and limitations for classroom use. We would like to share a chatbot creation experience, which we spent one hour building, with a 30-minute presentation. For each chatbot, we will explain its intended purpose, target users, basic specifications, and expected classroom applications. We will also describe the development process, including how the presenters designed the chatbot instructions, refined prompts, and adjusted the chatbot behavior through iterative testing. After introducing these three examples, the workshop will discuss the potential benefits of custom chatbots. In particular, we will show how they can help users access relevant information more efficiently, provide more focused guidance than general-purpose AI tools, and support educators who want to create AI-assisted learning environments tailored to specific instructional goals. The workshop will critically examine current limitations. Even after repeated tuning, custom chatbots may still produce inaccurate, incomplete, or contextually inappropriate responses. Therefore, developers and educators remain responsible for checking the accuracy of the content and deciding whether the chatbot output is appropriate for learners. By combining demonstration, reflection, and critical discussion, this workshop aims to help participants understand how custom chatbots can be used responsibly and realistically in educational settings.

items.title: Designing Teaching Materials with GenAI: Perceptions of Cognitive Load and Learner Competencies in Higher Education
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to design instructional materials in higher education, yet limited evidence exists on students’ perceptions of the cognitive demands and learner-related competencies involved. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory, this study examined university students’ perceptions of GenAI-supported instructional material design according to gender, age, and admission grade. A quantitative, non-experimental, ex post facto study was conducted with 451 university students enrolled in education-related undergraduate and master’s programmes. The instrument assessed perceived usefulness, beliefs concerning metacognitive practices, prior knowledge, and problem-solving strategies, and perceived intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load. Participants generally reported positive perceptions. Female students reported significantly higher scores on the metacognitive skills, prior knowledge, and problem-solving skills dimensions, although effect sizes were small. These differences should be interpreted cautiously, given that female students represented 82% of the sample. No statistically significant gender differences were detected in the cognitive load dimensions. Age showed only a weak negative association with extraneous cognitive load, whereas admission grade was positively associated with metacognitive scores in both gender groups and with prior knowledge and problem-solving scores among female students. The findings describe students’ beliefs about the practices and cognitive demands associated with GenAI-supported material design and may inform training in the critical review and pedagogical adaptation of AI-generated teaching materials.

items.title: Designing with Intent: A Comparative Analysis of Custom AI Chatbots as UDL-Aligned Tools for Multidisciplinary Instruction
items.abstract: The growing presence of AI in higher education has prompted instructors to move beyond passive adoption, to deliberate theory-grounded design. This session presents two custom AI chatbots (DisneyBot and Rico) developed within a teacher preparation course as the technology-enhanced component of a multidisciplinary instructional unit. DisneyBot is built on the ChatGPT platform to guide learners through an exploration of Disney parks, and Rico, is built on the Gemini platform as an interactive guide to information about Puerto Rico by scaffolding learning across four subject-specific lesson modules – Social Studies, ELA/ENL, Science, and Spanish. Both chatbots were developed to support differentiated and interactive learning for 4th and 5th grade students through a virtual field trip framework, with the broader goal of connecting classroom content to authentic real-world experiences. The design of each chatbot was grounded in UDL principles (CAST, 2018). Rather than serving as static information repositories, the chatbots were intentionally designed to function as interactive instructional mediators which use prompting inquiry, guiding subject-specific exploration, and offering differentiated entry points for learners with varying needs and language backgrounds (Vygotsky, 1978). The differences between the two platforms, in terms of interface architecture, customization depth, persona design, and interaction affordances, form the basis of a comparative analysis that will anchor the session. Participants will interact directly with both chatbots, examine the instructional design decisions behind them, and leave with a working framework for developing purpose-built AI chatbots that can be tailored to their own teaching contexts and disciplines.

items.title: Detecting Trade-Based Money Laundering in the Documents Themselves: A Cross-Validation Graph with Closed-Loop Self-Iteration
items.abstract: Trade-based money laundering (TBML) hides in the documents of trade rather than in the payments that settle it. Conventional transaction-monitoring systems examine amounts, frequencies, and velocities, and are therefore blind to the documentary substance of a shipment; machine-learning systems trained on transaction-level features inherit the same blindness; and static models of either kind decay as laundering typologies migrate across goods, corridors, and forgery techniques. This paper describes a detection system, disclosed in U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 64/170,275, that is organised around the documents themselves. Heterogeneous trade documents — commercial invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations, packing lists, letters of credit, and associated payment records — are parsed into canonical shipment assertions that retain provenance metadata, and entity mentions across documents are resolved to canonical identities, with alias collisions preserved as signals rather than merged away. The resolved material is assembled into a heterogeneous entity–document–shipment graph whose edges are of two kinds: documentary edges recording what each document declares, and consistency edges — computationally verifiable assertions linking attributes across documents that purport to describe the same shipment — each carrying a consistency score. From this graph the system computes features that encode known TBML typologies at the documentary level: unit-price deviation against benchmark price distributions indexed by HS code, trade corridor, and time window; cross-document quantity and value reconciliation; circular-trading cycles; phantom-shipment document asymmetries; and shipment-structuring patterns. A calibrated scoring model emits per-shipment and per-entity risk scores with machine-readable documentary reason codes, exposed through a real-time scoring API designed for pre-settlement interception. Investigation outcomes — suspicious activity report filings, confirmed typologies, and analyst labels — close the loop: confirmed activity reweights the suspicious-entity subgraph and re-runs community detection, labelled cases retrain the model, an active-learning strategy allocates analyst review by uncertainty over graph neighbourhoods, and per-corridor stationarity testing of benchmark price distributions detects typology drift and triggers benchmark re-estimation, targeted labelling, and model refresh — all without manual feature re-engineering. A further embodiment extends the graph across the full lifecycle of direct-to-consumer cross-border e-commerce. The paper reports no evaluation and no measurements; numerical values cited are the design targets and structural parameters stated in the disclosure.

items.title: Developing Rubrics for Evaluating Evidence Quality, Logical Soundness, and Cognitive Engagement in Debate and Argumentation-Based Training
items.abstract: Debate and argumentation exercises are widely used in higher education and professional training to develop critical thinking, yet their outcomes are often assessed with general, subjective criteria. This study aims to develop and validate an analytic rubric that integrates three constructs—evidence quality, logical soundness, and cognitive engagement—for evaluating performance in debate and argumentation-based training. An integrative design was employed, comprising theoretical analysis of existing evaluation systems, construct and descriptor development, expert review by five specialists in education and logic, and a pilot study in which two independent raters assessed 30 university students during a debate exercise. The final rubric comprises three constructs and nine criteria, each with level-specific descriptors. Experts rated its content completeness, precision, and applicability highly (mean 4.6 on a 5-point scale). The pilot study showed high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.85) and substantial inter-rater agreement, confirming the rubric’s reliability and objectivity; the comparatively lower scores on logical soundness indicate a priority area for instruction. The rubric functions not only as an assessment instrument but also as a diagnostic and formative tool that clarifies expectations for learners and guides instructors in planning debate-based teaching. Rater training and further adaptation to different age groups, debate formats, and AI-assisted assessment are recommended.

items.title: Development and Evaluation of AI-Integrated Digital Learning Modules for Food and Beverage Operations Under the Strengthened Senior High School Tech-Pro Curriculum
items.abstract: This study developed and evaluated artificial intelligence (AI)-integrated digital learning modules for Food and Beverage Operations under the Strengthened Senior High School Tech-Pro Curriculum. Using a developmental-descriptive research design with a one-group pretest–posttest quasi-experimental component, it involved 84 Grade 11 learners and five TLE/TVL teachers from five public secondary schools in Agusan del Sur, together with three expert validators. The modules were examined in terms of instructional features, competency alignment, validity, and acceptability. Expert evaluation questionnaires, teacher and student acceptability questionnaires, and achievement tests supplied the data, which were analyzed using means, standard deviations, mean percentage scores, independent-samples t-tests, and a paired-samples t-test. The six instructional feature dimensions were rated highly evident (means = 4.60–4.80), and the five validity dimensions were assessed as highly valid (means = 4.67–4.80). Teachers and students considered the modules highly acceptable, with no statistically significant differences in their ratings across the five dimensions (all p > .05). The reported mean percentage score rose from 69.4 on the pretest to 78.0 on the posttest. The paired comparison of achievement-test scores was statistically significant (t = −11.303, p < .001). The findings support the modules’ suitability as supplementary, competency-aligned learning resources, while the one-group design limits causal interpretation. Continued refinement, responsible AI-use guidance, and testing in additional instructional settings are recommended.

items.title: Development of a KYTC Highway Geometric Design Workshop
items.abstract: In-depth knowledge of geometric design principles is a prerequisite for delivering road projects that provide safe and efficient multimodal mobility for all users. Historically, Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) early-career design staff arrived at the agency with little design experience. The agency has relied on a combination of short courses and mentorship provided by experienced personnel to bring early-career design staff up to speed on design best practices. However, this approach to training carries limitations. Employee turnover and imposing workloads make it challenging for early- and even mid-career design professionals to receive guidance from seasoned designers who have long tenures at KYTC. And it hinders efforts to implement a consistent design philosophy across the agency. Recognizing that young designers, as well as project managers and project reviewers, would benefit from a course focused on geometric design, Kentucky Transportation Center (KTC) researchers worked with Cabinet staff to develop and deliver the Roadway Geometry Fundamentals Course. This five-day training introduces participants to a mix of foundational concepts (e.g., horizontal and vertical alignment, sight distance, cross-sectional elements, speed management, intersection design, roadside safety) and advanced topics (e.g., innovative design, context classification, human factors). The course blends instructor-led lectures, group exercises, and discussion to achieve learning objectives. A pilot version of the course was delivered in October 2025, and multiple offerings are planned for 2026. Long term, KYTC views the Roadway Geometry Fundamentals Course as an important vehicle for achieving agencywide consistency in design practice and elevating Kentucky to a position of national leadership in innovative design and road safety.

items.title: Development, content validation, and pilot application of an instrument for assessing healthcare waste management performance in hospital care
items.abstract: Healthcare waste management directly impacts patient safety, occupational health, and healthcare quality. Despite regulatory frameworks, healthcare institutions frequently encounter operational barriers due to unstandardized practices, insufficient continuous training, and limited managerial diagnostic tools. This study aimed to develop, content-validate, and pilot-test the Healthcare Waste Management Assessment Instrument (IAGRAS) as a decision-support tool for hospital governance and quality improvement. A mixed-methods study was conducted at a tertiary-level accredited hospital in Brazil. IAGRAS was structured around seven key performance indicators using an ipsative scoring system adapted from the Competing Values Framework. Content validity was evaluated by an expert panel using the Content Validity Index (CVI). A pilot application was performed with 50 nursing and hygiene professionals. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the D'Agostino test, Coefficient of Variation, and sector-specific performance mapping using BioEstat 5.0. Expert evaluation confirmed 100% agreement, yielding a CVI of 1 across all seven indicators. Pilot data demonstrated normal distribution (p>0.05). The overall performance mean reached 36% for the 'High Degree' knowledge category. Significant sector variations were identified: the Surgical Center (50%) and Hygiene/Cleaning department (43%) achieved the highest compliance scores, whereas the 4th-floor (26%) and 5th-floor (27%) surgical wards revealed major knowledge gaps regarding waste management plans, transport logistics, and regulatory standards. High Coefficients of Variation (up to 79.7%) highlighted substantial perceptual heterogeneity among staff. IAGRAS proved to be a content-valid and feasible diagnostic instrument for identifying operational bottlenecks and guiding targeted educational and administrative interventions in hospital settings. Its integration into routine institutional audits can strengthen hospital governance, biosafety culture, and care quality.

items.title: Dialysis Clinic Patient Flow and Work Design
items.abstract: Problem Definition: For 433,000 patients in the United States with advanced kidney failure, hemodialysis is a life-sustaining treatment. Approximately 7,600 outpatient dialysis clinics serve these patients, whose treatments cost over $25 billion annually. Each treatment involves a pre-treatment “put-on” task and a post-treatment “take-off” task performed by patient care technicians (PCTs). These frontline workers face intense, overlapping demands that can compromise patient safety and contribute to PCT burnout. We study how to jointly schedule PCTs and patients to reduce makespan and increase labor efficiency in dialysis clinic operations through better patient flow. Methodology/Results: We first analyze the prevailing “push” approach, which starts put-ons as soon as a technician and station are free. We then propose two alternatives: an “interlaced” scheme that staggers put-ons and take-offs to reduce idle time, and a “tandem” scheme that pairs two PCTs — one specializing in put-ons and the other in take-offs — across twice as many stations. We derive closed-form expressions for each approach’s makespan under constant treatment durations and show that interlaced schedules achieve the shortest completion time, whereas tandem configurations can reduce labor per patient. We also incorporate heterogeneous treatment durations and stochastic task times and arrivals to show numerically that our insights are robust. Managerial Implications: In contrast to the push-focused approach, these insights direct facility administrators’ attention to the primary driver of labor efficiency: minimizing the time that stations sit unoccupied between successive patients. Due to the inefficiencies of the push approach for a single pod, transitioning to an interlaced or tandem system while increasing the standard time allotted for tasks can alleviate workplace stress and promote patient safety without increasing labor costs. Specifically, dialysis clinic managers could move from the common 15/15-minute put-on/take-off scheduling standard to a 25/20-minute standard, thereby allotting PCTs 50% more time to complete tasks. We then propose two alternatives: an “interlaced” scheme that staggers put-ons and take-offs to reduce idle time, and a “tandem” scheme that pairs two PCTs — one specializing in put-ons, the other in take-offs — across twice as many stations. Under standard conditions, we derive closed-form expressions for each approach’s completion time and show that interlacing finishes earliest with homogeneous treatment durations, while tandem configurations can lower labor per patient. We also incorporate heterogeneous treatment durations to show numerically that our insights are robust. Managerial Implications: In contrast to the push-focused approach, these insights direct facility administrators’ attention to what is most important for labor efficiency: minimizing the time that a station is unoccupied between successive patients. items.title: DIDACTIC POSSIBILITIES OF USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN MOTHER TONGUE LESSONS
items.abstract: This article examines the didactic possibilities of using artificial intelligence technologies in the organization of mother tongue lessons, their role in the educational process, and their influence on the development of students' knowledge. It analyzes the opportunities offered by artificial intelligence tools for taking individual learning needs into account, differentiating language-related tasks, developing written and oral communication skills, and assessing learning. It also addresses pedagogical appropriateness, the reliability of information, and the need to maintain teacher oversight when introducing these technologies into mother tongue education. The article substantiates that the effective use of artificial intelligence can increase students' interest in language learning and help accommodate individual differences in the learning process.
